recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No core FHIR source change is recommended for FHIR-13656; any future extension visibility adjustment should be considered through the later FHIR-16525/FHIR-20637 design family and the FHIR Extension Pack linkage.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-core change request asking that standard extensions be made more visible because readers often missed resource-specific standard extensions; the reporter suggested either a table on the content page or a prominent link from the resource structure content to the standard extensions for that profile/resource.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied by SVN revision 12640, represented in git as 65beab7892f222ac4460dcfd25ab40c007777c0b, which added a resource content-page link from the alternate/additional definitions paragraph to each resource's profiles/extensions page. Later template history preserved that behavior by replacing the literal link with the generated [%ext-link%] placeholder and moving the template from source/template.html to tools/templates/template.html.
additional_context: FHIR-16525 revisited the same visibility concern and rejected listing all standard extensions inline as too prominent/noisy, preferring visible links near the resource content. FHIR-20637 then accepted the Zulip option to add a link to extensions below the content view. Current rendered resource pages link to Profiles and Extensions in the page tabs, include below-structure "See the Extensions" links, and retain the additional-definitions "see the extensions" link generated from the current template.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current build-scope resource template still carries the extension-link placeholder in the Additional definitions area, and current rendered Patient and Observation pages demonstrate the resource-level extension links that satisfy the seed request without adding redundant tables or prose.

related_jiras.note: Revisited listing standard extensions on resource content pages and narrowed the preferred design from an inline table to visible links.
Accepted a linked Zulip option to highlight extensions below the resource content view, reinforcing that current link-based visibility is intentional.
